clue.text: Son of Atalanta to some extent chicken to sue OAP wrongly

parts.note: to some extent means partly, in part
a hen is a female chicken

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of the words that follow are set out in a mistaken order

explanation.surface: An absurd picture of a cowardly man suing a pensioner by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges SUEOAP into OPAEUS. Parthenopaeus, one of the Seven against Thebes, was in some versions the son of Atalanta.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend this hero, one of the Seven against Thebes, is called Atalanta's child.

clue.text: Posthumous records of club activities

parts.note: the clue paraphrases the full title of Dickens's first novel, The Posthumous Papers of the Pickwick Club

explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's novel is formally titled as the posthumous papers of a club and records its members' travels.

clue.text: Sort of spin recommended by former MP for Oldham

definitions.text: Sort of spin recommended by former MP for Oldham

parts.words: Sort of spin recommended by former MP for Oldham
parts.note: a spin is a short ride; William Cobbett, once MP for Oldham

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' suggests politics or cricket, but here it is a jaunt on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobbett's book title pairs this countryside adjective with rides, and a spin is an outing.

clue.text: Atlas was used by Hercules to help him scrump their apples

definitions.text: Atlas was used by Hercules to help him scrump their apples

parts.words: Atlas was used by Hercules to help him scrump their apples
parts.note: in myth Hercules got Atlas to fetch the golden apples from the garden of the nymphs who guarded them; to scrump is British slang for stealing fruit from orchards

explanation.definitionFit: These nymphs tended the garden of golden apples that Hercules had to take as his eleventh labour.

clue.text: Composition of such pep by baroque musician

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of music written by a baroque composer with plenty of pep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition of' rearranges SUCHPEP. Johann Christoph Pepusch arranged the music for The Beggar's Opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepusch was a German-born composer working in London in the early eighteenth century.

clue.text: Can she the bodiless dead 7?" S. T. Coleridge, Christabel

definitions.text: Can she the bodiless dead 7?" S. T. Coleridge, Christabel

parts.words: Can she the bodiless dead 7?" S. T. Coleridge, Christabel
parts.note: a quotation with its last word blanked: the line in Coleridge's poem Christabel ends with a verb meaning catch sight of, and the 7 stands for the gap

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation clue; the printed 7 marks the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means to catch sight of, which is what the poem asks whether the mother's ghost can do.

clue.text: Stet obeli, possibly marginal note from lenient editor

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Proofreading marks and a lenient editor's comment in the margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges STETOBELI. Stet is the proofreader's mark meaning leave it as it was; obeli are dagger marks.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor content to allow something might write a phrase meaning allow it to stand, like stet.

clue.text: Legendary king in university, and the royal writer, become tedious

parts.note: R stands for royal, as in RN or RAF
a pen is a writing instrument
to drag on is to go on so long as to bore

explanation.surface: A royal author at a university whose work gets boring.
explanation.walkthrough: Uther Pendragon is King Arthur's father in legend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian tales he is the father of Arthur and a king of Britain.

clue.text: He takes to the air in test film?

definitions.meaning: a trial episode made to test a television series

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an aviator flying a plane and a trial programme made before a series is commissioned.

clue.text: Broad frame for novice playwright

indicators.note: a frame goes round a picture, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: broad means wide
L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A wide picture frame made by an inexperienced dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde wrote The Importance of Being Earnest and other comedies for the stage.

clue.text: George Russell includes afterthought as church feature

indicators.note: includes says the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: the Irish poet George William Russell wrote under the pen name AE
PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: An Irish poet adds a note as he describes part of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' signals the container. George William Russell, the Irish poet and mystic, signed his work with those two letters, a pen name crosswords borrow.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the vaulted recess at the east end of a church, behind the altar.

clue.text: "Great formal wigs, with behind" (from 1D)

parts.note: a quotation from the Dickens novel at 1-down with a gap between with and behind: the wigs had a ribbon knot at the back

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing words go between 'with' and 'behind'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing words name a ribbon fastening, a kind of knot worn at the back of an old-fashioned wig.

clue.text: Very small home, say, to the value of Scott castle

indicators.note: say signals that the words before are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a kennel is a tiny house for a dog
worth means having the value of

explanation.surface: A tiny house worth a certain sum, compared with a castle in Scott.
explanation.walkthrough: Kenilworth is a novel by Walter Scott named after the Warwickshire castle where it is set.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Scott's novel takes its title from the ruined castle in Warwickshire, England.

clue.text: Outspoken article from 28's author

parts.note: outspoken means candid, frank
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A frank essay by a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw wrote both the play at 28 and Candida, so the definition is a work by him.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernard Shaw wrote this play too, so it comes from the same pen as the play at 28.

clue.text: Laureate likened it to a sweet pain in the heart"

definitions.text: Laureate likened it to a sweet pain in the heart"

parts.words: Laureate likened it to a sweet pain in the heart"
parts.note: a poet laureate described a longing for the past as a sweet ache; the Greek roots mean homecoming plus pain

explanation.definitionFit: The word combines Greek roots for return home and pain, an ache of longing for the past that is also pleasant.

clue.text: Squire Headlong never could bear it

definitions.text: Squire Headlong never could bear it

parts.words: Squire Headlong never could bear it
parts.note: Squire Headlong in Peacock's novel Headlong Hall insists that guests drain their glasses and leave no dregs in the bottom

explanation.definitionFit: This is the liquor left at the bottom of a glass, which Peacock's hard-drinking squire would not tolerate.

clue.text: Author of Pantomime at the post office (the back door)

parts.note: G. B. Stern wrote the novel Pantomime

explanation.surface: A novelist turns up at the post office by the rear entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the' places the author's name after PO. G. B. Stern was an English novelist whose first book was Pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a small rear or side gate, especially in a castle or town wall.

clue.text: Final release of vehicle in bad rain

indicators.note: in places the vehicle inside the rearranged letters
bad says the letters of the next word are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A van finally gets away after being caught in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' signals the anagram, giving NIRA, and 'in' puts the vehicle inside it. Buddhism's goal is release from rebirth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism this is the state of final liberation from the cycle of rebirth.

clue.text: Peninsular war featured in fiction by Beryl Bainbridge and George MacDonald Fraser

definitions.text: Peninsular war featured in fiction by Beryl Bainbridge and George MacDonald Fraser

parts.words: Peninsular war featured in fiction by Beryl Bainbridge and George MacDonald Fraser
parts.note: not the Peninsular War against Napoleon but the 1850s war on a Black Sea peninsula, the setting of Bainbridge's Master Georgie and Fraser's Flashman at the Charge

explanation.walkthrough: 'Peninsular war' points to Wellington in Spain, but it means a war fought on a peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1853-56 conflict took place on the Black Sea peninsula and is the setting of both novels.

clue.text: Thoreau's cloak to take off

parts.note: a cape is a sleeveless cloak
to cod is to mock or parody, to take off

explanation.walkthrough: Henry David Thoreau wrote a travel book called Cape Cod.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoreau's travel book is named after the Massachusetts peninsula he walked.

clue.text: Theatre piece by Beckett

parts.note: Samuel Beckett wrote a short drama whose title is simply the general word for a drama

explanation.definitionFit: Beckett's one-act drama for three figures in urns bears the plainest possible title for a stage work.

clue.text: Snare devised by Jacobson

definitions.meaning: Dan Jacobson's first novel, The ..., set in South Africa

explanation.definitionFit: A snare catches animals, and Dan Jacobson wrote a novel with that title.

clue.text: 20 sort of strife will include returned example — you could put money on it

definitions.text: you could put money on it

indicators.note: will include says the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: the answer at 20-across names a kind of war, so its sort of strife is a war

indicators.note: returned says the abbreviation is turned back to front

parts.note: eg is short for for example

explanation.surface: A conflict containing a reversed case; something you could bet on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the abbreviation round and 'will include' signals the container. The 20 points to the Crimean, a kind of war.
explanation.definitionFit: A bet is a stake of money laid on an outcome.

clue.text: One of McMurtry's endearing endings?

parts.note: Larry McMurtry wrote ... of Endearment, and a limit or ending is another sense of the word for one of those

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a limit or end, and in the plural it begins McMurtry's novel title about endearment.

clue.text: Some hero guesses where the knave is

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hero tries guessing where a scoundrel is hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a dishonest man, a scoundrel.

clue.text: Corresponding with Jennings?

parts.note: a word meaning in agreement with, which precedes to in a phrase crediting a writer named Jennings

explanation.definitionFit: Followed by with, the word means agreeing or in keeping with something.

clue.text: Virgil starting to make play pleasant

definitions.meaning: the opening words of the Aeneid, arma virumque cano, translated
Shaw's comedy, one of his Plays Pleasant

explanation.definitionFit: Shaw took the title of his comedy from the English of the Aeneid's first words; it appears in his Plays Pleasant.
